sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Satish Jain - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Madhusudan Yadav - G.A. for respondent/State.

2] This is the first application filed by the applicant un the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail as he is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.119/2025 registered at Police Station Jawad, District Neemuch for the offence punishable under Sections 420,
465, 466, 467, 471 & 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3] The allegation against the applicant is of forgery of various documents, including the certificate of Pattas.

4] Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has already filed a complaint to the concerned police station, one year prior to the lodging of the FIR, i.e., on 03.04.2024, and the FIR has been lodged on 06.03.2025.
It is further submitted that till date the Handwriting expert's report is also not received.

In such circumstances, applicant's, who was NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:17254 2 MCRC-17738-2025 posted as Panchayat Secretary, arrest would not be necessary.
5] Counsel for the State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer, however, it is not denied that the Handwriting expert's report has still not been received.

6] In view of the same, this Court is inclined to allow the present application as the Handwriting expert's report has still not been received, despite the fact that the FIR has been lodged on 06.03.2025.

7] Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application Shyamsukh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72458899/
1 is allowed.

sentences.text: It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant shall be released on bail, upon his executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand only) and furnishing one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
He shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

However, it is also directed that subsequently, if the Handwriting expert's report is received by the respondent, and the same is found to be against the applicant, the respondent shall apply for the cancellation of bail, if so advised.
8] Accordingly, MCRC stands allowed.

( SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Pankaj Shyamsukh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72458899/
